s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive facial swelling with orbital involvement and neurologic deficits
salient_findings: Painless, bony-hard swelling of the left cheek
Numbness of the left cheek and weakness in movement of the left upper lip
Expansion of the left maxillary ridge with mobility of primary teeth
Large, well-circumscribed, expansile, heterogeneous mass in the left maxillary sinus
key_facts: 9-year-old boy with left cheek swelling and hyperglobus of the left eye
Hyperglobus first noted 1 year earlier
Swelling of the left cheek developed 6 months later
Marked progression of swelling over the preceding 3 months
Normal overlying skin
Numbness of the left cheek and weakness in movement of the left upper lip
No other neurologic deficits, no visual disturbances, and ocular motility intact
Expansion of the left maxillary ridge with mobility of primary teeth c, d, and e
Large, well-circumscribed, expansile, heterogeneous mass in the left maxillary sinus
Deviation and destruction of the nasal septum
Invasion of the ethmoid sinus
Thinning, displacement, and perforation of the anterior wall of the sphenoid sinus
Destruction of the pterygoid plates
Elevation and perforation of the left infraorbital rim
Extreme postero-superior displacement of the second molar toward the inferior orbital fissure
Compromise of the nasopharyngeal space
Seasonal allergic reactions and glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase deficiency
WBC 19 × 10³/μl, RBC 3.66 × 10⁶/μl, hemoglobin 10.6 g/dl, hematocrit 33.2%, and MCHC 31.9 g/dl

shortlist.label: Cherubism
shortlist.why_kept: Characterized by bilateral enlargement of the jawbones, which matches the patient's presentation of cheek swelling and hyperglobus of the eye

shortlist.label: Fibrous dysplasia
shortlist.why_kept: Can cause facial asymmetry and swelling, and may involve the maxillary sinus, consistent with the patient's symptoms and imaging findings

shortlist.label: Juvenile ossifying fibroma
shortlist.why_kept: A type of fibro-osseous lesion that can occur in the jaw and cause swelling and facial asymmetry, similar to the patient's presentation

shortlist.label: Central giant cell granuloma
shortlist.why_kept: Can cause jaw swelling and expansion, and may involve the maxillary sinus, which aligns with the patient's clinical and radiographic findings

shortlist.label: Ewing sarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: A malignant bone tumor that can cause rapid growth and destruction of the jawbones, which could explain the patient's rapid progression of symptoms and aggressive imaging findings

raw.rationale: The patient's age, sex, and clinical presentation of bilateral cheek swelling and hyperglobus, along with the radiographic findings of a well-circumscribed, expansile, heterogeneous mass in the maxillary sinus, are consistent with Cherubism. The condition typically presents in childhood, with a male predominance, and is characterized by bilateral expansion of the jawbones, which matches the patient's symptoms.

rejected.label: Fibrous dysplasia
rejected.why: While fibrous dysplasia can cause expansile lesions, it typically presents with a ground-glass appearance on radiographs, which is not mentioned in the case.

rejected.label: Juvenile ossifying fibroma
rejected.why: This condition can cause aggressive jaw lesions, but it is less common and typically presents with more rapid growth and destruction.

rejected.label: Central giant cell granuloma
rejected.why: This lesion can cause jaw expansion, but it is typically more aggressive and has a different radiographic appearance.

rejected.label: Ewing sarcoma
rejected.why: This malignant tumor can cause rapid jaw destruction, but it is typically associated with systemic symptoms and a more aggressive clinical course, which is not mentioned in the case.
